function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Here’s a quick rundown of the most common ways to get a cake delivered—plus a few extra tips to make sure it arrives fresh and on time:

| Option | How it works | Typical delivery area | What to look for |
|--------|--------------|-----------------------|------------------|
| **Local bakery** | Call or visit the bakery’s website; place an order in‑person or online. | Usually same‑city or within a 30–60 mi radius. | Check reviews, ask about custom designs, confirm pickup/delivery windows. |
| **Grocery store** | Many supermarkets (Kroger, Safeway, Publix, Whole Foods, etc.) have a baked goods section and offer curbside pickup or delivery through their own app or third‑party services. | Same‑city, often part of the store’s regular delivery zone. | Look for “Fresh Bakery” or “Cakes & Pastries” sections; ask about special orders. |
| **Online cake shops** | Sites like Goldbelly, CakeDelivery.com, or local boutique bakeries ship nationwide. | Nationwide (shipping may take 1–3 days). | Verify shipping dates, packaging, and whether they accept custom orders. |
| **Food‑delivery apps** | DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub, Postmates, and SkipTheDishes partner with local bakeries and restaurants that offer cake delivery. | Depends on the restaurant’s delivery radius (often 10–20 mi). | Use filters for “Desserts” or “Bakery”; read ratings and delivery fees. |
| **Specialty cake makers** | Companies such as Magnolia Bakery, Levain Bakery, or local artisan bakers often have dedicated e‑commerce sites. | Usually local or regional; some ship nationally. | Ask about custom flavors, sizes, and shipping insurance. |
| **Subscription services** | Monthly cake clubs (e.g., “Cake Club”) deliver a new cake each month. | Varies; many are nationwide. | Check subscription terms, cancellation policy, and flavor variety. |

### Quick Tips for Ordering

1. **Know the deadline** – Most bakeries require orders at least 24–48 hours in advance for custom cakes.  
2. **Specify the occasion** – Mention birthdays, anniversaries, or corporate events so the baker can suggest appropriate designs.  
3. **Ask about shipping** – If you’re ordering online, confirm the packaging method (foam boxes, insulated bags, etc.) and whether the cake is shipped frozen or refrigerated.  
4. **Check the return policy** – Some sites allow you to cancel or modify orders up to a certain point before shipping.  
5. **Use local review sites** – Yelp, Google Reviews, and Facebook can give you real‑time feedback on quality and service.  

### Need a Recommendation?

If you let me know your city or zip code, I can pull up a list of top-rated local bakeries and their delivery options right now. Just drop your location, and I’ll fetch the latest data for you!
